title: Split a task's raw user prompt into userDescription, separate from the agent-derived description
userDescription: when using 'create-task', take the user's description and add it to the task as key: 'userDescription', separate from the 'description' key.  the description key should be the derived/flushed out description generated by the agent.  this separates the user's prompt from the agent's understanding. the current behavior is to put the user's description at the beginning of the 'description' field and then put two new lines and then put the agent's understanding of the task.

"") and scripts/viewTaskHook.ts (line 11). Treat 'userDescription' as optional, since every existing task in tasks.json and completedTasks.json predates it and has only 'description'.

No migration of existing task records is required or wanted — old tasks keep their combined 'description' and simply have no 'userDescription'.

userDescription: a task needs a 'version' key.  'create-task' should provide it. version comes from the latest commit hash of the active branch.  parsing of tasks based on version key value comes later, in a separate codebase addition.
description:
Scope is deliberately write-only: create-task records the key, nothing reads it yet. No consumer, no validation, no backfill of the tasks already in .taskTools/tasks.json — a task without a version key stays without one, and every reader must tolerate its absence. The `version` key does not appear anywhere in .taskTools/tasks.json today.

Two files change. skills/create-task/template/taskTemplate.json gains a `"version"` entry (place it next to `taskNumber` at line 2, since both are machine-supplied rather than authored). skills/create-task/SKILL.md gains two lines: an injection alongside the existing one at line 7 — line 7 is currently `- taskNumber to use: !`node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/nextTaskNumber.ts"`` — plus a "Populate `version` with ..." instruction near the existing ones at lines 21-23.

Nothing needs resolving the way nextTaskNumber.ts resolves the task-file location; it is one git command, and the injection already runs with the user's project as its working directory, which is the repo whose HEAD is wanted — not the plugin's own repo. title: Let the planner report missing files, append them to tasks.json, regenerate the brief, and retry planning

description:

Lines 74-87 fan out over TASKS and bucket results into plans / planned / needsClarification / notRelevant. The consequence observed in practice: a planning run for task 64 returned needs-clarification purely because the reference scripts it needed to read were absent from the owned list, and a human had to widen the list and relaunch the workflow by hand.

Work to do:

1. Add an optional `missingFiles` array of repo-relative path strings to PLAN_SCHEMA in skills/tackle-tasks/plan.workflow.js, and extend the plannerBrief text so the agent is explicitly told: when the blocker is access rather than ambiguity, return status 'needs-clarification' with missingFiles populated and question explaining why each path is needed.

2. Add a new script, scripts/addTaskFiles.ts, that is the only thing which mutates tasks.json here — the workflow must shell out to it rather than editing JSON inline. CLI shape should follow the existing convention in scripts/getTaskDetails.ts and scripts/unblockDependents.ts: parse the leading task number(s) from process.argv.slice(2) using leadingTaskNumbers() from scripts/taskFiles.ts, then take the paths to append. Locate tasks.json with resolveTaskFiles() and read with readTaskFile() (scripts/taskFiles.ts:16-24, 39-47, 49-56). Append only paths not already present (de-duplicate, preserve existing order), and write back with JSON.stringify(tasks, null, 2) + "\n" to match scripts/taskArchival.ts:38-71 and scripts/unblockDependents.ts:13-25. Expose or reuse this so the plan workflow can rewrite the single brief after the file list grows, rather than re-running the whole prepare step.

4. In plan.workflow.js, on a needs-clarification result that carries a non-empty missingFiles, run addTaskFiles for that task number, regenerate its brief, and re-run runPlanner once with the updated list. Cap the retries (one extra planning attempt is enough) so a planner that keeps asking for more files cannot loop forever; if the second attempt still returns needs-clarification, fall through to the existing needsClarification bucket unchanged. Note this retry is a distinct concept from the existing retryAgent helper at lines 59-66, which only guards against a null harness result — do not overload it.

- The repo has no modifiableFiles/readOnlyFiles split today; `files` is the single ownership fence, consumed both by declaredFiles() in prepareTasks.ts and as the "owned files" text in plan.workflow.js:28. title: Have the commit-message subagent collect the staged diff itself instead of receiving it from the main agent
userDescription: make the commit-message subagent always get the latest git changes programmatically, instead of from the main agent, because the main agent's repo view goes stale after 1 conversation turn.
description:
The commit-message subagent must run the git commands itself, at the moment it starts, rather than being handed a diff the main agent captured earlier. The main agent's view of the repository goes stale as soon as anything else is staged, so a diff passed in as prompt text describes a snapshot that may no longer match HEAD's index.

Observed in a real run of this pipeline: the commit-message subagent was launched, and tasks 58, 59 and 60 were staged afterwards. The returned message described neither of them and mischaracterised the code change it did see. Nothing errored — the message was simply wrong, which is the dangerous failure mode, because a wrong-but-plausible commit message gets used.

The wording that causes this is in skills/tackle-tasks/COMMIT_MESSAGES.md: "give it the staged diff of every affected repo — collected after staging with git -C <repo> diff --staged ...". "Give it" puts the collection in the caller's hands and makes the diff prompt text. Rewrite so the subagent is instructed to run `git -C <repo> diff --staged -- ':(exclude)*tasks.json' ':(exclude)*completedTasks.json' ':(exclude)plans/archived'` itself, along with whatever it needs to enumerate the affected repos and detect a moved submodule pointer. The caller should pass repository paths, not diff contents.

skills/update-tasks/SKILL.md line 27 has the same defect and is vaguer still — it says to use a Sonnet 5 subagent to summarise "the work done" without saying where the diff comes from at all. Point it at COMMIT_MESSAGES.md rather than restating the procedure, so there is one source of truth.

Note that scripts/stage-and-summarize-stop.ts (line 36) inlines COMMIT_MESSAGES.md into a Stop hook, and skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md (line 141) does the same, so both pick up the corrected wording automatically with no edit of their own. skills/close-tasks/SKILL.md line 22 is unaffected: it uses a fixed "Closed tasks [...]" message and no subagent.
tests: in a throwaway repo, stage a change, spawn commit-message subagent, then make the commit with the subagent's message, then make another change, stage that 2nd change, spawn commit-message subagent again, and make sure the subagent's message is different (because the diff contents are different)
closureNote: Commit-message subagent now runs git diff --staged itself against caller-supplied repo paths and detects moved submodule pointers via raw mode 160000; update-tasks SKILL.md now points at COMMIT_MESSAGES.md as the single source of truth. Codex approved after one plan revision, group-1 tests green.

title: Investigate why runMergePhase reported merged while publishing nothing, leaving the source branch without the work
description:
Investigate why runMergePhase reported merged while publishing nothing for recent runs of /tackle-tasks [n..] valid.

Observed on 2026-08-06: runMergePhase.ts printed {"status":"merged", ...,"publicationTargets":[]} and runState.status "approved", and mergeTaskWorktrees did commit tasks 59 and 60 onto branch task-group-1 (commits f798ced, 1ad8763) and onto the operation branch operations/mshpovbw-gr8sjg9nq3j/parsed-github-com-matkatmusic-tasktools-572765a1-c8146a02, but the source branch new-usage-graph never received the work.

The run pinned baseOid 99517e72ac5f8afffef2d9d627764dc08f4eb863 at start, and new-usage-graph advanced past it mid-run (commit dc1ec9e at 09:12, then 4a723f4 and 4fa5a4a from a concurrent session), so the branches diverged and the consolidation-back-to-source-branch step that produced commits like 58b4b8d runConsolidation in the previous run did not happen.

Two questions to answer:

1. Why publicationTargets was empty and judgeMergeRun still returned merged.

2. Whether a source branch that moved past the pinned baseOid should make the merge report blocked, or should instead trigger a rebase or re-consolidation, rather than silently reporting success.

Relevant files: scripts/runMergePhase.ts (buildMergeOutcomes, judgeMergeRun), scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, scripts/mergePipeline.ts.

A merge that reports merged while the user checkout does not contain the code is the dangerous case, because the orchestrator then invokes close-tasks and the task is archived as finished even though the work never reached the user's branch.
tests: End-to-end drift test in tests/runMergePhase.test.ts: 1. init a throwaway repo and commit A, so baseOid = A. 2. build pipeline args pinned to baseOid A. 3. commit B on the source branch, simulating the concurrent session that caused this bug. 4. run runMergePhase. Assert either status !== "merged", OR git log <sourceBranch> contains the task commits. That is, "merged" must imply the user's branch actually has the code.
closureNote: Root cause found and fixed: judgeMergeRun in scripts/runMergePhase.ts now returns blocked when the merge script exits clean with an empty publicationTargets, so a run whose source branch drifted past its pinned baseOid can no longer be reported as merged and archived while the user branch lacks the code. Both brief questions are answered in plans/task-63-plan.md. The requested automatic rebase-then-retest-then-retry recovery was rejected twice by codex as under-specified and is filed as task 88. Verified: typecheck clean, full suite 1117/1117 pass.

title: Fold unblockDependents into the closeTasks script so closing and unblocking happen in one call
userDescription: unblockDependents.ts should be part of the close-tasks script execution that moves entries from tasks.json to completedTasks.json, and not invoked by the agent directly.  Note: when create-task becomes dynamic-injection-based and is refactored, this task might be automatically handled.
description:
Current state, after task #64 landed scripts/closeTasks.ts (114 lines):

- `closeTasks(taskNumbers, closureNote, projectRoot, commitHashes)` at scripts/closeTasks.ts:36-82 resolves both file paths with `resolveTaskFiles`, reads both files, filters out ineligible numbers into `skipped` (52-57), resolves every note/hash up front so a missing Record entry throws before anything is written (59-65), splices each task out of `tasks` and pushes it onto `completedTasks` (67-74), then writes BOTH files once at 76-79 guarded by `if (closed.length > 0)`. Returns `{closed, skipped}` (type at 5-8). The CLI entry is at 102-114.
- scripts/unblockDependents.ts (25 lines) then re-reads and re-writes tasks.json a second time. Its own header comment at lines 1-3 already states it is "Invoked by the close-tasks skill after moving closed tasks to completedTasks.json".
- skills/close-tasks/SKILL.md:20 is the prose that makes the agent run it as a separate step.

**The blocking structural problem:** unblockDependents.ts exports nothing. Every line of it is top-level module-scope code that runs on import — argv parsing at line 7, the usage/exit guard at 8-11, `resolveTaskFiles(process.cwd())` at 13, the mutation loop at 16-23, the conditional write at 24, and the stdout report at 25. `closeTasks` cannot call it as-is; importing it would execute it. The logic must first be extracted into an exported function (taking the closed numbers and a project root, returning the unblocked task numbers) before it can be folded in.

**Decision taken:** keep scripts/unblockDependents.ts as a file. It retains its CLI entry point and gains that exported function, which closeTasks imports — one implementation, two entry points. tests/unblockDependents.test.ts (48 lines) stays pointed at the extracted function. Do not delete the file; a way to unblock without closing something is worth keeping.

**Second reason this matters beyond tidiness — the double write.** Today tasks.json goes through two independent read-modify-write cycles: closeTasks writes it at scripts/closeTasks.ts:77, then unblockDependents re-reads it at line 14 and rewrites it at line 24. Anything that touches tasks.json between the two sees a half-applied state, and an agent that forgets step two leaves stale blockedBy entries pointing at completed tasks. Fold the unblock pass in BEFORE the write at closeTasks.ts:76-79 so both mutations land in a single write of the in-memory `tasks` array. Do not call the extracted function in a way that re-reads the file — pass it the already-loaded array.

**Also update** skills/close-tasks/SKILL.md:20 to drop the separate invocation instruction, and fold what it reported ("removed closed task(s) from blockedBy of task(s): ..." / "no blockedBy references to the closed task(s)", unblockDependents.ts:25) into closeTasks's own stdout at closeTasks.ts:110-113, so the user still sees what was unblocked. Consider adding the unblocked numbers to `CloseTasksResult` (closeTasks.ts:5-8) rather than only printing them.

**Ordering notes, none of them hard blockers:**
- Open task #69 also edits scripts/unblockDependents.ts (it changes blockedBy entries to `{taskNum, reason}` objects, rewriting the filter at line 18). Either order works — whichever lands second edits the logic in its new home — but expect a rebase.
- Open task #71 copies the close-tasks SKILL.md body verbatim into a script. This task should land FIRST, or #71 will faithfully copy the now-wrong line 20 instruction into the new brief.
- The user's own note about a later dynamic-injection refactor possibly absorbing this work refers to that same family (#71 for close-tasks, #72 for create-task). Those tasks are explicitly scoped as verbatim copies with no logic changes, so they will NOT absorb this one — this change has to be made deliberately.

**Line budget:** closeTasks.ts is at 114 of a 250-line cap, so the extracted call plus reporting fits comfortably.
tests: One-call close-and-unblock. In a temp repo, close task M in a single closeTasks call where another task lists M in blockedBy. Assert M landed in completedTasks.json AND the dependent's blockedBy lost M — both after one invocation, with tasks.json written once, not twice. Cover the field-drops-when-empty case (a dependent blocked only by M ends with no blockedBy key at all) and the partial case (a dependent blocked by M and another still-open task keeps the other entry).
closureNote: Folded unblockDependents into closeTasks as an exported pure function so closing and unblocking land in one write of tasks.json; unblocked numbers now surface in CloseTasksResult and CLI stdout, the standalone CLI is kept, and close-tasks SKILL.md drops the separate step.

title: Give split-task a free-text guidance argument that drives both the child descriptions and the file split
userDescription: add a 'guidance' param hint to 'split-task <taskNum> <count>', so that you can provide guidance to the agent on how to split the task.  example: 58's title has 2 jobs: split task file ownership, make briefs point at files. I would like to be able to invoke the skill as 'split-task 58 2 make splitting task-file ownership one task and making briefs point using filepaths the other task'
description:
The split-task skill from task #65 has landed: skills/split-task/SKILL.md (28 lines), scripts/splitTask.ts (177 lines), tests/splitTask.test.ts.

**Current state.** SKILL.md:4 declares `argument-hint: "<taskNum> <numSplits>"`. Line 7 shells out to `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/splitTask.ts" info $1 $2`, and line 9 restates the two positional values. The file grouping is computed entirely by `partitionFiles` (splitTask.ts:27-42), which slices the parent's `files` array into N CONTIGUOUS, near-equal chunks by position — `base = Math.floor(files.length / numSplits)`, remainder distributed to the earliest groups. SKILL.md:13 states the consequence plainly: "The file grouping itself is fixed by the command's output; the only decision here is which piece of work (child description) goes with each group." Children are then matched to groups strictly in order (lines 13, 15, 19, 25), and `closeParentTask` (splitTask.ts:115-132) recomputes the same partition and calls `verifyChildFiles` (101-113) per child, throwing unless each child's `files` array matches its positional group exactly, element for element.

**Why a guidance string alone would not work.** The user's own example asks that one child take the file-ownership work and the other the briefs-point-at-filepaths work. Those pieces of work almost certainly do not correspond to a contiguous slice of the parent's `files` array, so under today's positional partition the guidance would be unhonourable — the agent would either ignore it or produce children that `verifyChildFiles` rejects at close time. Any change that adds the argument without addressing the partition is cosmetic.

**Decision taken: guidance drives the file split too.** The agent proposes which files belong to which child based on the guidance, rather than receiving a fixed positional partition. Validation shifts from "matches the contiguous slice" to "is a valid partition of the parent's files" — which the codebase already has: `validateFileGroups` (splitTask.ts:44-67) checks exactly the three properties that matter, reporting files assigned to more than one child (49-52), files not in the parent's array (54-57), and parent files missing from every group (59-62). That function becomes the real gate; `partitionFiles` becomes a fallback for when no guidance is given, not the authority.

**Work to do:**

title: task-stats prints each blocked task's collapsed blocker chain plus the fastest unblocking sequence
userDescription:
add the blockedBy sequences of every blocked task to the output of task-stats.  '[a] <- [b,c] <- [d]' shows 'd' is blocked by 'b,c', and either 'b' or 'c' is blocked by 'a'. 
it should also show a 'fastest unblocking sequence: tackle-tasks [n,m,o...]' where 'n,m,o' are the left-most nodes of each blockedBy sequence.  Note: the printout shouldn't duplicate information: It should NOT print out (one per line) '[a] <- [b]', '[b] <- [d]', '[c] <- [d]', '[a] <- [b,c] <- [d]'.  For these 4 tasks, it should only print out the single line "sum".
description:
**Where it goes.** scripts/taskStats.ts already computes blocking but only as a count — `blockedCount` at :68, derived from `openBlockersOf` at :24-27, which resolves ONE level of blockedBy and filters to still-open numbers. The chain data is a new field on the `TaskStats` type (:5-20) computed in `computeTaskStats` (:59-82) and rendered in `formatTaskStats` (:84-102), which already builds a string array and joins it. The CLI at :104-109 needs no change.

**The collapse rule, stated as an algorithm.** Emit one chain per SINK — an open task that has at least one open blocker and that no other open task lists as a blocker. Walk backwards from the sink one level at a time: level N-1 is the union of the open blockers of every task in level N, minus any task already seen. Render as `[level0] <- [level1] <- ... <- [sink]`, each level a comma-joined ascending list in brackets. Because a non-sink blocked task always appears inside some sink's chain, it never gets a line of its own, which is exactly the no-duplication requirement. Guard the walk with a seen-set so a blockedBy cycle terminates instead of looping.

**The roots line.** `fastest unblocking sequence: tackle-tasks [n,m,o...]` where the numbers are the union of every chain's level0, deduplicated and sorted ascending, comma-joined with no spaces so the string can be pasted straight into the tackle-tasks invocation format documented at skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md:12.

**Verified against real data.** Running this algorithm over tasks.json at the time of writing yields sinks 36, 83, 84, 96, 97, 105, 106 and these seven lines: `[35] <- [36]`, `[82] <- [83]`, `[75] <- [84]`, `[93] <- [96]`, `[93] <- [97]`, `[86] <- [105]`, `[107] <- [106]`, with `fastest unblocking sequence: tackle-tasks [35,75,82,86,93,107]`. Note that 96 and 97 are distinct sinks sharing root 93, so two lines with the same level0 are correct output, not a duplication bug — the rule dedupes chains that are sub-paths of other chains, not chains that share a root.

**The format is deliberately lossy and that is fine.** `[a] <- [b,c] <- [d]` asserts only that some member of level N is blocked by some member of level N-1, not that every pair is connected. The user chose this compression knowingly; do not add per-edge annotation to make it exact.

**Duplication worth folding in.** `openBlockersOf` now exists three times with the same body: taskStats.ts:24-27, scripts/checkBlockers.ts:13-17, and scripts/runStartup.ts:12-14. Task 84 independently needs the same transitive walk and the same `<-` rendering for its hook short-circuit output, and its description already asks for the walk to be extended in one shared place rather than reimplemented. Whichever of 84 and 108 lands first should export the shared walk; the second reuses it. Not blocking in either direction.

title: Populate operationBranch before any merge attempt so the base-drift auto-retry can actually run
userDescription: The base-drift auto-retry in scripts/runMergePhase.ts can never succeed on a first drift, because rewriteOperationBranches fail-closes on an operationBranch that was never populated. Repro from run msj8czjj-r3odjv8prf8 on 2026-08-07: the merge phase returned blocked with error 'an occurrence operationBranch does not carry the expected prefix "operations/msj8czjj-r3odjv8prf8/"'. Chain of causes, all verified in source: prepareTasks.ts (and repositoryDiscovery.ts) initialize every occurrence's operationBranch to the empty string when writing .taskTools/run-arguments.json. mergePipeline.ts never persists a real operationBranch back into that file - operationBranches.ts recomputes branch names from runId plus occurrenceId in memory on every invocation and never reads the persisted field back. coordinateMergeRetry at runMergePhase.ts lines 160-166 calls rewriteOperationBranches, which returns null the moment any occurrence's operationBranch does not start with operations/{oldRunId}/, and a null return becomes a blockedVerdict. Therefore on any run that hits base drift before a successful push - which is exactly the first-drift case - operationBranch is still the empty string and the retry is guaranteed to block. Note the earlier steps of coordinateMergeRetry do work: rebaseGroupOntoSource rebased the group cleanly and the post-rebase suite passed before the guard rejected it. plans/task-91-plan.md shows the fail-closed guard was a deliberate design decision from a prior review pass, so this is a design gap to close rather than a typo to patch. Three candidate fixes were identified and the choice is open: (1) let rewriteOperationBranches pass an empty or never-assigned operationBranch through unchanged so first-drift retries proceed, which loosens the deliberate guard; (2) keep the guard and accept manual out-of-band retry, which is what was done to land task 77; (3) fix it upstream so prepareTasks.ts / repositoryDiscovery.ts populate a real operationBranch before any merge attempt, making the guard's invariant actually true. Option 3 looks the most correct because it makes the guard honest instead of weakening it. Files likely involved: scripts/runMergePhase.ts, scripts/prepareTasks.ts, scripts/repositoryDiscovery.ts, scripts/operationBranches.ts, scripts/mergePipeline.ts, tests/runMergePhase.test.ts. Impact: every tackle-tasks run whose base branch moves mid-run - common when a second session is committing - blocks at merge and needs a hand merge.

title: Stop archiving tasks against commits that do not contain their code, and gate archival on the merge phase actually succeeding
userDescription: The merge pipeline archives a task as completed against an empty consolidation commit even when the merge phase then reports blocked, so a task can read as done while none of its code is in the tree. Observed on 2026-08-07 in run msj8czjj-r3odjv8prf8 for task 77. What happened, all verified against git: mergeTaskWorktrees.ts produced commit 844bf46 titled runConsolidation msj8czjj-r3odjv8prf8: integrate parsed-github-com-matkatmusic-tasktools-572765a1. That commit is empty - git show --stat shows no file changes at all - and git cat-file -e 844bf46:scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts fails, so it does not contain any of task 77's three files. Despite that, the pipeline moved task 77 out of tasks.json into completedTasks.json with completionDate 2026-08-07, commitHashes [844bf46], and closureNote absent entirely (jq reports null). runMergePhase.ts then returned status blocked for the same run. So the archival happened on a run that the merge phase itself judged unsuccessful, and it recorded a hash proving nothing. Task 77's code only reached new-usage-graph because it was hand fast-forwarded from task-group-1 afterwards as commit 17b6c6e; without that manual step the task would have been permanently marked done with its work stranded on an unmerged branch. Two separate defects are worth fixing together: (a) archival must not run, or must be rolled back, when the merge phase reports blocked - the consolidation and the closure should share one success gate; (b) a consolidation commit that integrates nothing should not be created, or at minimum should never be recorded as a task's completion hash - record the commit that actually carries the task's declared files, and verify those paths exist in it before writing commitHashes. A cheap invariant to enforce: before archiving task N with hash H, assert every path in that task's files array exists in H (git cat-file -e H:path), and refuse to archive otherwise. Note this is distinct from task 108, which is about the base-drift retry being unable to run; this one is about closing tasks against commits that do not contain their code, and it is the more damaging of the two because it silently loses work. Files likely involved: scripts/mergePipeline.ts, scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts, scripts/runMergePhase.ts, scripts/taskArchival.ts, scripts/closeTasks.ts, tests/mergePipeline.test.ts, tests/taskArchival.test.ts.

title: Stop stagedDiffs.ts excluding tasks.json so a task-only change still produces a commit message
userDescription: the commit-message skill deliberately excludes tasks.json, so it will see an empty diff. So a task-only change produces no message at all, and there's no subagent to spawn because there's nothing to summarize. the empty-diff case above means any close-tasks or create-task run gets a blank commit message.  This causes the main agent to produce the diff message.  fix: update the skill to stop excluding tasks.json.  Blocked by the task to inject the diff directly into the subagents promt.
description:
The exclusion lives in exactly one place: `EXCLUDES` at scripts/stagedDiffs.ts:5, holding `:(exclude)*tasks.json`, `:(exclude)*completedTasks.json` and `:(exclude)plans/archived`. It is spread into both git invocations in that file — the diff itself at :8 and the `--raw -z` scan for moved submodule pointers at :12. Only the :8 use matters for this fix; the :12 use is a pathspec on a submodule-pointer scan, where task files are irrelevant either way, so unexcluding is harmless there.

The blank result is produced at stagedDiffs.ts:38, `if (diff.trim().length > 0)`, which suppresses the entire `=== repo ===` section when a repo's filtered diff is empty. A staging set consisting only of task files therefore yields zero bytes on stdout, and skills/commit-message/SKILL.md:10 — which instructs the agent to hand "the diffs above" to a Sonnet 5 subagent — has nothing to hand over. Confirmed by direct observation: several task-only sessions in a row produced no commit message at all.

History of the exclusion: it is inherited verbatim from the pre-skill era. The identical three-pathspec list appeared in skills/tackle-tasks/COMMIT_MESSAGES.md, which task 62 deleted when it converted that document into skills/commit-message/. The list was never re-justified for the skill; it was copied.

Decision and open point: remove `:(exclude)*tasks.json` only, as the user specified. `:(exclude)*completedTasks.json` is a judgment call the implementer should settle and state — completedTasks.json is 222KB and its diffs are proportionally large, but a close-tasks run stages BOTH files simultaneously, so leaving it excluded means such a run is summarised from the removal side alone. That is still a non-empty, summarisable diff, so it is not a blocker either way. `plans/archived` should stay excluded; that directory does not exist and the entry is inert.

Size is not a concern for tasks.json itself: the file is 134KB but a single create-task addition diffs to roughly 18 lines and a closure to a similar size, because the array is pretty-printed one field per line.
tests: In a throwaway git repo: stage a change to .taskTools/tasks.json and nothing else, run stagedDiffs.ts, and assert stdout is non-empty and names the tasks.json path — the case that produces a blank commit message today. Add a second case staging both tasks.json and completedTasks.json together, which is what a close-tasks run does, and assert the output is still not blank. Keep a negative case proving the change did not unexclude everything: stage a file under plans/archived alone and assert stdout is still empty.

title: Generate a task's brief and plan inside its worktree and delete them before merge, so git never tracks them
userDescription: remove brief-N.md and task-N-plan.md from the plans/ when task N is closed via '/close-tasks'.
description:
**The problem.** Closing a task leaves plans/brief-N.md and plans/task-N-plan.md behind forever; nothing removes them, so plans/ only grows — 142 files against 53 completed tasks when first reported, and worse since. Both paths are minted in scripts/prepareTasks.ts: the brief at :104 (`join(repoRoot, "plans", \`brief-${taskNumber}.md\`)`) and the plan at :170 (`join(repoRoot, "plans", \`task-${number}-plan.md\`)`), both rooted at the MAIN repo, so every run writes them into a git-tracked directory (164 of the 173 files in plans/ are tracked today).

**Approach decided with the user — do not just delete on close.** These artifacts are per-run scratch, so they should never enter the main repo in the first place. Root briefFile and planFile at the group's WORKTREE rather than repoRoot, so each run's artifacts live beside the code being changed and outside the tracked tree. Then delete them inside the worktree immediately before the merge step, so git never captures them at all. Nothing downstream hardcodes these paths — plan.workflow.js:41-44 and verify.workflow.js:23 both take briefFile/planFile from the prepared arguments — so the change is contained to where the paths are built and where the merge is driven.

**Depends on the per-task-worktree rewrite.** Task 86 restructures tackle-tasks so each unit gets its own workflow, and task 104 renames worktrees by task number; until a task reliably has its own worktree, "write the brief into the worktree" has no stable destination. Blocked on 86 for that reason.

**The merge path closes tasks too, and closeTasks.ts is not on it.** archivePublishedTasks in scripts/taskArchival.ts:38 does its own tasks.splice / completedTasks.push at :60-64 — it never calls closeTasks(). mergePipeline.ts:236 invokes it on the success path. So any cleanup wired only into scripts/closeTasks.ts silently misses every task closed by a merge, which is the normal path. Whatever removal helper this task adds must be reachable from both.

**run-*.json are already handled on the happy path.** mergePipeline.ts:237 already does `rmSync` over resolveRunArgumentsPath / resolveRunOutcomesPath / resolveStepOutputsPath after a successful publish. The residue comes from runs that block or fail before reaching that line. Under this task's design those files move into the worktree alongside the brief and plan; note that task 104 also re-keys them, so whichever lands first, the other adjusts.

**The existing backlog is a separate, git-visible problem.** The 164 already-tracked plan files cannot be made to vanish by a plain delete — removing a tracked file IS a git change. Drain them with `git rm`, on every invocation rather than as a one-shot migration: for each task number already in completedTasks.json, remove plans/brief-N.md and plans/task-N-plan.md if present. That is the same drain-on-every-invocation pattern task 98 uses for the legacy files key, so the backlog clears itself over the next few closures with nothing to remember. Do not move them to plans/archived — that directory does not exist, it appears only as a pathspec exclude in the commit-message tooling, and the user chose deletion; git history retains them.

**Two correctness constraints for the removal itself.** A missing file is not an error — a task closed without ever being planned has neither file, and may have one but not the other, so use existence-tolerant removal. And match exact filenames only: plans/ holds unrelated documents such as 'amended task 13.md', plans/tackle-metrics.jsonl and plans/tackle-tasks-v2.md, and a number-prefix collision must not bite either — closing task 1 must not touch brief-10.md or brief-100.md.

Related but not blocking: task 87 makes plans/brief-N.md strictly derived and rebuilt on every plan launch, which is consistent with treating it as disposable scratch.
tests: Three checks. (1) Placement: prepare a run for task N and assert the returned briefFile and planFile both resolve inside that group's worktree, not under the main repo's plans/, and that after preparation the main repo's plans/ contains no brief-N.md or task-N-plan.md. (2) Pre-merge removal: write both files in the worktree, drive the merge step, and assert both are gone from the worktree before the merge commits — so a `git status` in the worktree shows them neither tracked nor untracked. (3) Backlog drain, exercised through BOTH closing paths: in a throwaway repo create plans/brief-N.md and plans/task-N-plan.md for a task already listed in completedTasks.json, then once close task N via closeTasks and once via archivePublishedTasks, and after each assert both files are gone AND the deletion is staged in git (not left as an unstaged working-tree change), that an unrelated brief-M.md is untouched, that brief-10.md and brief-100.md survive closing task 1, and that a task with no plan files closes without throwing.

title: Name worktrees, branches and run files by task number so concurrent tackle-tasks sessions cannot collide
userDescription: it's possible for multiple sessions to use the same worktree group. find a way to ensure sessions never use the same worktree group when multiple sessions are active and running tackle-tasks simultaneously (maybe a lock file or job tracker file)
description:
**Root cause.** Every shared name in a run is derived from `groupId`, and `groupId` is just `index + 1` (scripts/taskGroups.ts:56), so it restarts at 1 on every run and carries zero cross-session uniqueness. scripts/prepareTasks.ts:134 builds the worktree path as `join(tmpdir(), "taskTools-wt", basename(repoRoot), \`group-${group.groupId}\`)` and prepareTasks.ts:95-97 builds the branch as `task-group-${groupId}`. Two sessions that start tackle-tasks on unrelated tasks both get group 1, therefore the same directory and the same branch.

**The collision is destructive, not merely shared.** createWorktreeForGroup (prepareTasks.ts:133-153) takes the `existsSync` path when the directory is already there and runs `git -C <worktree> checkout --force -B <branch> <currentBranch>` (:138-142). That force-resets the branch to the source-branch tip, discarding whatever the other live session had committed there. The comment on :137 shows the intent was reusing a worktree left by an EARLIER, finished run; it does not distinguish that from a run still in flight.

**Why groupId was chosen originally, and why the fix is still safe.** A group is not one task — TaskGroup carries `taskNumbers: number[]` (taskGroups.ts:8-13) because groupTasksByFileOverlap bundles tasks that share files and therefore must be implemented in one tree. groupId was the only single scalar a group had, and it arrived in the first commit that added the file (6b8fe68, "Step 3: add scripts/prepareTasks.ts"), never revisited for concurrency. But a stable per-group identifier already exists: members are sorted ascending (taskGroups.ts:50) and groups are sorted by their lowest member (taskGroups.ts:55), so `taskNumbers[0]` is deterministic for a given group.

**Decided with the user.** Name by task number, not by a lock: worktree `taskTools-wt/<repo>/<taskNum>` and the matching branch, using the group's lowest task number. This removes the collision by construction for sessions working different tasks, and as a bonus makes a re-run of the same task reuse its own worktree instead of whichever slot index it happened to land in.

**Residual case that must not be silently force-reset.** Two sessions running the SAME task number still resolve to one worktree. That is a genuine conflict — same task, same files. Replace the unconditional `checkout --force -B` with a check: reuse the worktree only when it is not owned by a live run, and otherwise fail with a clear error naming the conflicting task, rather than destroying commits. This is the only place a lock-like signal is needed, and it is far narrower than a general job tracker.

**Run artifacts collide the same way, and are in scope.** resolveRunArgumentsPath / resolveRunOutcomesPath / resolveStepOutputsPath (prepareTasks.ts:77-89) are three fixed paths under `.taskTools/`, written at prepareTasks.ts:221-223 and runMergePhase.ts:64-66 and deleted at mergePipeline.ts:238. Two concurrent runs in one repo overwrite each other's pipeline state. Open point for planning: a run spans SEVERAL groups, so a single group's task number cannot name it — pick one scheme and apply it consistently, either the run's lowest task number across all its groups or a per-run subdirectory such as `.taskTools/runs/<key>/`. The existing `runId` (prepareTasks.ts:68-70) is already carried in run-arguments.json and is available as that key if a task-number-derived name proves ambiguous.

**Blast radius.** Only two source files construct these names — scripts/prepareTasks.ts and scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts — but the run-file paths are consumed by scripts/mergePipeline.ts and scripts/runMergePhase.ts, and a dozen test files hard-code `task-group-N` strings as fixtures. Cleanup must also be revisited: worktrees keyed by task number accumulate one directory per task rather than one per slot index, so stale ones need sweeping.
tests: Two-session collision test: prepare two runs over different task numbers against the same repo, back to back without cleanup in between, and assert they receive different worktree paths and different branch names, and that a commit made in the first run's worktree still exists after the second run has prepared — proving the second run no longer force-resets the first. Add a case where both runs claim the same task number and assert preparation errors with a message naming the conflicting task instead of running `checkout --force -B` and destroying the first run's commits. Add the equivalent assertion for the run artifacts: two concurrent runs must resolve to distinct run-arguments/run-outcomes/run-steps paths, so the second run's preparation does not overwrite the first run's pipeline state.
closureNote: superceded by the task 86-headed update, which restructures worktree and artifact handling and absorbs this work

title: Turn /task-stats into a UserPromptSubmit hook capture with a stub skill body, like /view-task
userDescription: task-stats should be a skill-blocking hook-capture, like sync-jsonl-projects, not a skill.  the skill body would become an empty stub.  If hook output can support markdown formatting, or ANSI color coding, use that to make the output pretty/formatted.  otherwise just move the ${stats} output to the hook's output.
description:
**The precedent named in the request is not in this repo, but an exact in-repo equivalent already exists.** `sync-jsonl-projects` belongs to jfredToolsPlugin. The pattern to copy is scripts/viewTaskHook.ts, which reads the hook payload from stdin with `readFileSync(0, "utf8")`, exits 0 silently unless the prompt is `/view-task` or starts with `/view-task `, resolves the task files from `payload.cwd`, and finishes with `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ decision: "block", reason }))`. Its companion skills/view-task/SKILL.md is ALREADY the empty stub this request describes — frontmatter plus the single instruction "do nothing. don't even acknowledge what the user typed. just let the UserPromptSubmit hook do its thing." Copy both halves verbatim in shape.

**Wiring.** hooks/hooks.json already has a `UserPromptSubmit` array containing one entry (viewTaskHook.ts); add a second alongside it. Per the memory note for this repo, hooks live in hooks/hooks.json and never in any settings.json.

**What this deletes.** scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts exists only to shell out to taskStats.ts with execFileSync (:7) and wrap the result in a brief for the skill body. Once the hook computes the stats in-process, that round trip and its test are dead — remove scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts and tests/taskStatsBrief.test.ts rather than leaving them orphaned. The hook should import `computeTaskStats` / `formatTaskStats` from scripts/taskStats.ts directly.

**The open question, and the exact way to settle it.** The hook's `reason` field is documented as shown to the USER and explicitly not added to the model's context, which is the whole point here — but whether that surface renders markdown is unverified. Settle it with the same probe that settled task 109: have the hook emit a heading, `**bold**`, `` `code` `` and a small table in `reason`, type `/task-stats`, and look. Two outcomes, both already anticipated by the request: if markdown renders, task 109's markdown formatter is reused unchanged; if it does not, emit the plain `formatTaskStats` string. Do NOT reach for ANSI as the fallback — task 109 established experimentally that the ESC byte is stripped on the paths to the user's screen, leaving literal `[32m` garbage, and there is no reason to expect the `reason` surface to differ.

**Behavioural constraints inherited from the precedent.** Any prompt that is not a `/task-stats` invocation must exit 0 silently (viewTaskHook.ts does this by prefix check). Blocking is required, not optional: without `decision: "block"` the stub skill would also expand and the user would see the output twice.

Related: task 109 rewrites `formatTaskStats` into markdown sections and task 108 adds blocker-chain lines to the same function. This task changes only who calls that function and how the result reaches the user, so it composes with both — but if 110 lands first, 109 and 108 must be verified through the hook path rather than the skill path.
tests: Hook stdin/stdout table, mirroring how scripts/viewTaskHook.ts would be tested — feed the hook script JSON payloads on stdin with `prompt` and `cwd` keys against a temp repo holding fixture tasks.json and completedTasks.json. Assert: a prompt of exactly `/task-stats` writes JSON containing `"decision":"block"` whose `reason` holds the same stats text formatTaskStats produces for that fixture; a prompt of `/task-stats ` with trailing arguments behaves the same; an unrelated prompt such as `/tackle-tasks [1]` produces no stdout and exit code 0; and a prompt merely containing the words task-stats mid-sentence is likewise ignored. Assert the reason is non-empty for a fixture with zero open tasks, so an empty backlog still reports rather than blocking with a blank message.
closureNote: Moved the /task-stats computation out of the skill body into a new UserPromptSubmit hook scripts/taskStatsHook.ts, stubbed skills/task-stats/SKILL.md, registered the hook alongside viewTaskHook in hooks/hooks.json, and deleted the dead scripts/taskStatsBrief.ts round-trip and its test in favour of tests/taskStatsHook.test.ts; merged as 284aa0e with typecheck clean and all three hook tests passing.

title: Detect destination-branch drift in the merge phase and rebase the worktree before merging instead of aborting the run
userDescription: merge workflow needs to check if the destination branch's commit the worktree was created from is still the tip of the destination branch or if the destination branch has new commits, and handle the 'new commits' situation appropriately (has merge conflicts ? rebase worktree and resolve conflicts before merge attempt : merge attempt)
description:
Root-cause findings from reading the merge subsystem:

**The base commit is never recorded at worktree-creation time.** scripts/prepareTasks.ts:133-154 `createWorktreeForGroup` cuts the branch with `git -C <repoRoot> worktree add -B <branch> <worktreePath> HEAD` (or, when the worktree directory already exists from a prior run, `git -C <worktreePath> checkout --force -B <branch> <currentBranchName>`). It returns only the path and never runs `rev-parse HEAD`. A base OID does exist in the system, but it comes from a different subsystem at a different moment: scripts/repositoryDiscovery.ts:39-49 and 89-118 capture `git rev-parse HEAD` per occurrence into `RepositoryOccurrence.baseOid` (type at scripts/repositoryManifest.ts:16-17), and prepareTasks.ts:194-212 `runAsCli` loads that manifest BEFORE calling buildWorkflowArguments, which is what creates the worktrees. The two are never re-synced, so today's `baseOid` is an approximation of the worktree's true fork point, not a record of it. It is persisted to disk in .taskTools/run-arguments.json under `repositoryManifest.occurrences[].baseOid` (prepareTasks.ts:77-79, 221-223), never as a git ref.

**There is no drift check between creation and merge — only a compare-and-abort at the point of no return.** scripts/basePublication.ts:48-53 `revalidateRecordedBaseOids` compares the recorded `baseOid` against `readCurrentRefOid(...)` (basePublication.ts:39-42) and, if the ref moved, aborts the whole publish with `published: false`. scripts/mergePipeline.ts:221 does the same inline: `if (readCurrentRefOid(...) !== occurrence.baseOid) return true;` — an abort. `publishCanonicalRef` (basePublication.ts:59-77) then relies on `git update-ref <ref> <target> <expected-old>` so git itself refuses on a race. Every one of these is compare-and-abort; none recomputes against the new tip and retries. That abort-the-run behaviour is exactly what this task replaces with reconciliation.

**Nothing named baseBranchResolution or baseReconciliation does what this task needs.** scripts/baseBranchResolution.ts `resolveBaseBranchCandidates` only answers which local branch name currently has tip == this OID, at discovery time. scripts/baseReconciliation.ts `checkBaseReconciliation` only settles disagreement between multiple occurrences of the same logical subrepo. Neither compares a worktree's fork point to a destination tip.

**`git merge-base` is invoked nowhere in the codebase, and `rebase` appears zero times** across scripts/, skills/ and tests/ (grepped). This task introduces the first use of both.

**Two distinct merge paths exist; be explicit about which one changes.**
- Path A — the one the tackle-tasks pipeline actually runs (runMergePhase.ts to `mergeTaskWorktrees.ts --run` to `runMergePipeline` in scripts/mergePipeline.ts) never calls `git merge`. **What reviewerBrief gives instead.** scripts/reviewPlanBrief.ts:39-113 exports `reviewerBrief(plan, target, amendment)`. It demands evidence citations for every flagged issue (line 65), forbids the reviewer from editing the plan and permits it to write only the amendment file (57), tells it to clear a pre-existing amendment before a re-review (61), and — critically — makes the verdict non-discretionary: the reviewer counts its durable fixes and runs `node <abs>/planReviewRuling.ts <plan> <fixcount>` (73-77), then copies the three printed lines verbatim into a structured amendment template (81-112). **The ruling.** scripts/planReviewRuling.ts:17-22 defines `Ruling` as ACCEPTED_AS_IS 0, APPLY_FIX_THEN_ACCEPT 1, APPLY_FIX_THEN_REREVIEW 2, REWRITE_THEN_REVIEW 3. 1. Planner produces the plan.
2. Review round (at most 2 reviews total, preserving the existing cap): reviewerBrief + codex produces a ruling.

description:
**Why here.** `scripts/checkBlockers.ts` is the first script every `tackle-tasks` invocation runs (see skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md, which calls it with `--unblocked` before `getTaskDetails.ts` and `prepareTasks.ts`), so a cycle detected there stops the run before any planning, worktree creation, or implementation cost is paid.

**The gap, confirmed by reading all three call sites.** `openBlockersOf` exists three times with effectively the same body and none of them recurse: `scripts/checkBlockers.ts:15-16` returns the full blockedBy entry objects filtered to open task numbers; `scripts/taskStats.ts:25-26` and `scripts/runStartup.ts:13-14` return just the numbers. Every one resolves exactly one level, so a back edge is indistinguishable from an ordinary dependency.

**Two downstream symptoms this prevents.** (1) Tasks in a cycle report BLOCKED forever with no unblocking path, and `tackle-tasks` refuses to run them without ever explaining why the blocker never clears. (2) Task 108 renders blocker chains by walking backward from sinks - an open task with open blockers that no other open task lists as a blocker. A pure cycle contains no sink, so those tasks are omitted from the chain output entirely while still counting toward `blockedCount`. Task 108 deliberately declined to solve this with strongly-connected-component sink selection (see the Declined review suggestion section in plans/task-108-plan.md); detecting and halting here is the cheaper answer, and this task is that answer.

**Live data checked before filing.** `.taskTools/tasks.json` at commit 28c852c: 36 open tasks, 8 with open blockers (36, 83, 84, 96, 97, 105, 106, 113), zero cycles found by depth-first search. This is a guard against a future bad hand-edit, not a repair of current state - so it must not change the exit code or output of any currently-passing run.

**Scope boundary.** Detection and halting only. Do not add SCC machinery, do not change chain rendering, and do not extract the duplicated `openBlockersOf` into a shared module - that dedup is separately noted in task 108 and task 84 as non-blocking in either direction.
